title: How to file a motor insurance claim in Kenya: a step-by-step guide
excerpt: Most claim delays in Kenya come from missing documents, not insurer slowness. This guide walks you through exactly what to prepare before you make the call.
author: ADT Motor Risk Team
content: Report the incident to your broker and insurer as soon as it is safe to do so. Note the time, location, vehicle details, and any third parties involved.
Take clear photos of vehicle damage, the scene, and relevant documents including your driving licence and logbook.
Complete the claim form accurately and attach the police abstract where required, repair estimates, and any witness statements.
Your ADT advisor can review your file before submission to reduce back-and-forth and speed up insurer assessment.

title: WIBA explained: who is legally required to have it and what it covers
excerpt: Work Injury Benefits Act cover is mandatory for all Kenyan employers with staff. Here is what the law requires, what it pays, and how to stay compliant without overpaying.
author: ADT Compliance Desk
content: WIBA provides compensation for work-related injuries, disabilities, and death arising from employment duties.
Employers with one or more employees are generally required to maintain WIBA-compliant cover under Kenyan law.
WIBA should be reviewed alongside employers liability and occupational safety policies to close gaps in workforce protection.
ADT helps businesses structure compliant WIBA cover and maintain accurate employee schedules at renewal.

title: Five ways SMEs can reduce insurance claim delays
excerpt: Slow claims are rarely the insurer's fault — they usually trace back to gaps in documentation at the time of the incident. Here is a practical pre-incident checklist.
author: ADT Advisory Desk
content: Assign one internal contact for all insurance incidents and keep policy schedules, receipts, and asset registers updated.
Report incidents within 24 hours even if you are still gathering internal records.
Use a simple checklist: photos, incident report, policy number, and contact details for all parties involved.
Work with your broker to pre-agree escalation contacts so claims receive immediate attention during business hours.

title: Marine insurance for importers and exporters: what to know
excerpt: Cargo moving through the Port of Mombasa faces specific risks that standard transit cover often misses. This guide covers what a proper marine policy should include.
author: ADT Corporate Risk Desk
content: Marine cargo policies protect goods against loss or damage during sea, air, and inland transit.
Importers and exporters should align cover with Incoterms, consignment value, and route-specific risks.
Document packing lists, bills of lading, and commercial invoices before shipment to support faster claims.
ADT advises on marine structures for SMEs and corporates moving goods across East Africa and global markets.

title: Group vs individual medical cover: which makes sense for your business?
excerpt: Group medical plans offer better rates per head but come with minimum membership requirements. This comparison helps you decide based on team size and budget.
author: ADT Health Benefits Team
content: Group plans suit employers offering inpatient, outpatient, and maternity benefits across a workforce with shared underwriting.
Individual and family plans offer flexibility for owners, freelancers, and dependants not covered by an employer scheme.
Compare provider networks, sub-limits, co-pays, and chronic condition cover before selecting a plan.
ADT helps growing teams design medical structures that balance cost, access, and renewal stability.

title: Pre-renewal checklist for corporate insurance buyers
excerpt: Renewing without reviewing is the most common way corporates end up underinsured. Use this checklist before your next renewal conversation to close coverage gaps.
author: ADT Corporate Risk Desk
content: Review your risk register against active policies and note new locations, assets, or contracts from the past year.
Update sums insured for inflation, equipment additions, and changes in headcount or turnover.
Analyse claims history and near-misses to adjust limits, deductibles, and cover extensions.
Confirm board, lender, and contractual insurance requirements are reflected in policy wording before renewal.
